articles.description:
In tutorials, ML looks simple:
train a model → get accuracy → ship.
In production, none of that survives contact with reality.
What actually determines whether a model runs in production is a set of trade-offs that are rarely taught:
latency · memory · inference cost
Accuracy matters - but only after these constraints are satisfied.
I didn’t understand this until I started building real systems.
Most ML education focuses on:
Algorithms

Math

Loss functions

Benchmarks



What it often underemphasizes:
Python overhead can dominate small or fast models

Floating-point math is not “free” at scale

Cache locality affects real latency

Serialization can cost as much as inference

P95 latency matters more than mean latency

Memory fragmentation hurts long-running services

Many production bugs …
articles.title: Production ML is not about models. It’s about trade-offs.

articles.author: Nikola Roganovic
articles.description:
Somewhere in your account, EC2 instances are running with no traffic, no purpose, and no owner.
These instances were born from lies.
They were launched for a “temporary test.”
Now they sit there.
Who approved them?
AWS charges you for your ignorance.
You tell yourself idle instances aren’t that expensive.
CPU at 1%.
You're still being charged.
Compute.
Idle infrastructure resources are not free.
You don’t get a discount for ignorance.
How many instances would vanish if “no traffic” was a deletion rule?  
If the answer scares you, good.  
Nobody logs into them.
But nobody deletes them either.  
Because deleting the wrong instance is dangerous.
So you choose fear over discipline.
If you can’t explain what breaks when it’s terminated, you already lost control.
You wouldn’t keep routing traffic to unhealthy instances.
But you ignore idle EC2 because the damage arrives monthly, not instantly.  
That doesn’t make it harmless.
You are not “scaling responsibly.”
So here’s the uncomfortable truth:
If you’re afraid to delete EC2 instances, you don’t understand your own system.
Now decide.
Keep paying for servers nobody needs.
For more stories like this, check out CostlyFY.
articles.title: You’re Running EC2 Instances That Do Nothing
